nodes.source_text: The HER performance of three hetero-interfaces, commercial Pt/C and Ru/C was evaluated using a three-electrode system in 1.0 M KOH electrolyte at room temperature. nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM and TEM images clearly show the NT structure with a diameter of about 174 nm and a wall thickness of about 22 nm (Figure 1b,c).

properties.description: High-magnification image showing nanofiber morphology with fibrous, interwoven structure

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms NT structure of MoO2@Ru NT.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM and TEM images clearly show the NT structure with a diameter of about 174 nm and a wall thickness of about 22 nm (Figure 1b,c).

properties.features: layered nanostructure with dark lines indicating lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM image of MoO2@Ru NT shows measured lattice spacings of 0.205 nm (Ru (101)) and 0.323 nm (MoO2 (011)), confirmed by SAED pattern.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1d is the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image for MoO2@Ru NT, the measured lattice spacings of 0.205 and 0.323 nm correspond to the Ru (101) and MoO2 (011) planes, respectively, which is in accordance with selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows Ru species mainly dispersed on the surface of MoO2@Ru NT.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high angle annular dark field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) image clearly shows numerous bright dots on the surface of NT, which manifests that Ru species are mainly dispersed on the surface of NT (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS elemental mappings show uniform distribution of Mo, Ru, O over MoO2@Ru NT; atomic ratio Mo:Ru = 71.5:28.5.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, STEM energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mappings show that the Mo, Ru and O elements are evenly distributed over MoO2@Ru NT (Figure 1f). The STEMEDS result indicates that the atomic ratio of Mo/Ru is 71.5:28.5 (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms Mo/Ru atomic ratio of 71.9:28.1 for MoO2@Ru NT.
nodes.evidence_snippet: similar as that (71.9:28.1) obtained from inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD: MoO2@Ru NT shows only MoO2 phase (JCPDS 78-1069); MoO2/MoO3@Ru NT shows MoO2 and MoO3 phases (JCPDS 85-2405); MoO3@Ru NT shows MoO3 phase. No Ru peaks observed due to low content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a, all diffraction peaks of MoO2@Ru NT are indexed to MoO2 (JCPDS No. 78-1069). For MoO2/MoO3@Ru NT, all diffraction peaks match well with standard patterns of MoO2 and MoO3 (JCPDS No. 85-2405), whereas the diffraction peaks of MoO3@Ru NT can be attributed to MoO3. It is worth noting that no peak belonging to metallic Ru was observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p XPS shows Ru0 (Ru0 3p3/2: 462.12 eV for MoO2@Ru NT, 462.44 eV for MoO2/MoO3@Ru NT, 462.90 eV for MoO3@Ru NT) and Ru4+ states. Higher BE for MoO2@Ru vs literature Ru metal indicates electron transfer from Ru to MoO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2b, the Ru 3p spectra of all three hetero-interfaces can be deconvoluted into two pairs of peaks, which are assigned to Ru0 and Ru4+. Notably, the binding energy of Ru0 3p3/2 for MoO2@Ru NT (462.12 eV) is significantly higher than that of metallic Ru nanocrystals reported in the literatures (i.e., 461.48 eV,[30] 461.6 eV[31]), which indicates electron transfer from Ru to MoO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES of MoO2@Ru NT positioned between Ru foil and RuO2, confirming Ru valence between Ru0 and Ru4+ and electron transfer from Ru to MoO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) at Ru K-edge indicates that the adsorption position of MoO2@Ru NT is situated between those of Ru foil and RuO2 (Figure 2c), which demonstrates that the valence state of Ru in MoO2@Ru NT is between Ru0 and Ru4+, further confirming the electron transfer from Ru to MoO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge EXAFS of MoO2@Ru NT shows Ru-O at 1.53 Å and Ru-Ru at 2.33 Å, verifying Ru-O-Mo interface. Lower coordination numbers vs Ru foil/RuO2 indicate unsaturated coordination environment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform extended Xray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectrum at Ru K-edge of MoO2@Ru NT (Figure 2d) displays two peaks at 1.53 and 2.33Å, which can be assigned to Ru-O and Ru-Ru bonds, respectively. The appearance of Ru-O bond verifies the existence of Ru-O-Mo interface in MoO2@Ru NT.

properties.type: Fourier Transform Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure

nodes.characterization_summary: WT-EXAFS of MoO2@Ru NT shows strong signal at 9.10 Å⁻¹ (Ru-Ru) and weak signal at 5.60 Å⁻¹ (Ru-O), confirming coordination environment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, the wavelet transform EXAFS (WT-EXAFS) analysis (Figure 2g-i) provides further evidence regarding the coordination environment of Ru in MoO2@Ru NT, which shows that one strong signal (9.10 Å⁻¹) and another weak signal (5.60 Å⁻¹) are observed, assigned to Ru—Ru and Ru—O bonds, respectively.
